xmldoc.short_description: Apply an inverse geometric transformation to points.

syntax.syntax_item: [u, v, w] = transformPointsInverse(tform, x, y, z)

param_input_item.param_description: Geometric transformation structure created by affine2d, affine3d or projective2d.
Coordinate arrays of identical size. Supply x and y for a 2-D transformation, or x, y and z for a 3-D transformation.
Packed point matrix with one column per dimension: N-by-2 for a 2-D transformation, N-by-3 for a 3-D transformation.

param_output_item.param_description: Transformed coordinate arrays, same size as the corresponding inputs.
Packed matrix of transformed points, same size as X.

description.p: Apply the inverse of the geometric transformation stored in tform to a set of points, using the row-vector convention [u ... 1] = [x ... 1] * inv(tform.T). For a projective transformation the result is normalized by its homogeneous coordinate.
Points can be given either as separate coordinate arrays of equal size, or as a single packed matrix with one column per dimension. It is the inverse operation of transformPointsForward.

example_item.example_item_description: Forward then inverse is a round trip
